title: The canonical full-column map to the odd quotient is a chain map
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $K$ an integer-indexed bicomplex of $A$-modules, $S_a$ short complexes of integer-indexed cochain complexes, and $e_a:(S_a).X_2\cong K^{-a,\bullet}$. Suppose $K^{p,\bullet}$ is zero for $p>0$. Use the explicit stages $F_n$, inclusions $s_n$, and column inclusions of [lem-pc-derived-total-filtration-stable]. For $j\in\mathbf N$, the maps from $(S_j).X_2^{k+j}$ to $\operatorname{coker}(s_{2j+1})^k$, obtained by applying $e_j$, restricting the full column inclusion to $F_{2j+2}$, and applying the cokernel projection, commute with the differential of $(S_j).X_2[j]$. This gives the canonical full-column cochain map. It kills $(S_j).f[j]$, and, if every $S_a$ is short exact, its unique descent through $(S_j).g[j]$ defines the canonical map from $(S_j).X_3[j]$ to the odd quotient.

proof.text: Membership in the range defining the stage restricts the full column map to stage 2j+2. The horizontal part of its total differential lands in an earlier full column for j>0; for j=0 it vanishes by the zero positive column hypothesis. The vertical part is the middle endpoint differential with the shift sign (-1)^j. After restriction, compose with the cokernel projection to kill the horizontal part and obtain the displayed chain-map equation. The lower-column generators lie in stage 2j+1, so the shifted first arrow is killed. Short exactness preserved by the shift functor supplies the unique descent through its epimorphic second arrow. All these calculations and the data construction are proved in Lean.
